facts.text: Early human settlement in Loures dates back to the Upper Paleolithic, with discoveries at the Cave of Pego do Diabo and the Cave of Salemas.
Neolithic burial chambers such as the Anta de Carcavelos and the Anta do Alto da Toupeira highlight the area’s ancient funerary landscape.
During the 1st millennium, Loures was a Roman settlement centered around a cemetery that later became the site of the first church.
After the Templars were disbanded in 1311, their lands in Loures passed to the Order of Christ, which rebuilt a church over a 4th‑century temple.
In 1598, the plague drove Lisbon residents to the elevated village of Montemor, where they built the Chapel of Nossa Senhora da Saúde for protection.
Loures achieved town status on 26 October 1926 and later became a city on 9 August 1990.
